subtopic: Learning to code from the internet
passage: For three months I watched coding videos every night. Loops, functions, lists: I nodded along and felt like I was getting somewhere. Then my cousin Sarika, who builds websites for a living, handed me her laptop with a blank editor and said, “Print the numbers 1 to 10.” I sat there for twenty minutes. When the tutor typed a loop it looked obvious. Alone, I couldn't type one. My face went hot and I felt stupid. Sarika didn't laugh. She said, “Watching isn't typing.” I realised I had not written a single line of my own in ninety days. I had only been following someone else's hands. — Deepak

qa.q: What did Sarika ask Deepak to do in the blank editor?
What did Deepak feel while staring at the blank editor?
qa.a: Embarrassed and shaken: Deepak felt hot and stupid because knowing a loop by watching was not the same as writing one.

qa.q: What could Deepak do instead, and why?
qa.a: Type each example, then close the video and rewrite it from memory, since writing it alone builds real recall.

qa.q: How does Deepak's habit look to Sarika?
qa.a: Sarika, who builds websites, has likely seen this before and does not laugh, but wants Deepak to see that watching is different from typing.

grounding: A student watches tutorial after tutorial, feels sure of learning, but cannot write a loop in a blank editor.

subtopic: Learning to code from the internet
passage:
Coding club note, Tuesday
In September Anirban told me he had finished forty hours of programming videos. He can name every topic: loops, functions, lists. Today I gave the group an empty editor and one task: print the numbers one to ten, then only the even ones.
Tarun finished in four minutes after two wrong tries. Anirban sat very still, then opened a video in another tab. I asked him to close it. For ten minutes he typed and deleted the same line. Finally he said quietly, “In the videos it just works. I always typed what they typed.”
That is the gap. Watching felt like learning, but he never had to produce code from nothing. I did not push it in front of the group. After club we agreed on one small exercise a day, written before any video, and he will show me on Thursday.
– Club mentor

qa.q: What task did the club mentor give the group?
qa.a: Print the numbers one to ten, then only the even ones, in an empty editor.

qa.q: What was Anirban probably feeling while typing and deleting the same line?
qa.a: He was likely embarrassed and confused, since forty hours of videos had made him feel ready and now nothing came out on his own.

qa.q: What could Anirban try instead of more videos?
qa.a: Write one small exercise a day before watching anything and use a video only to get unstuck, so the typing comes from his own thinking.

qa.q: How might Tarun see Anirban's struggle?
qa.a: Tarun might be surprised, since Anirban can name every topic, and may realise that Tarun's own two wrong tries were part of the learning.

grounding: Shows the cost of tutorial hopping without practice: a student who watched many videos cannot write a simple loop in an empty editor.

subtopic: Learning to code from the internet
passage:
Saturday night
Worst evening. Chetan bhaiya came home from his hostel and I bragged that I've been learning to code for two months. Which is true, I've watched maybe sixty videos. He opened his laptop, made a new empty file and said, “Write something that counts the words in this sentence. Any way you like.”
I stared. I knew the words “split” and “loop” from videos. I didn't know where to put them. In every video someone else typed first and I copied. Here nobody typed first.
Chetan bhaiya didn't laugh. He said, “Watching isn't the same muscle.” He showed me nothing, just asked me to try one line and run it. It broke. The second line broke too. After forty minutes it counted the words. Forty minutes for four lines.
Tomorrow: no videos until I've written something myself.
– Kiran

qa.q: What did Chetan bhaiya ask Kiran to write?
qa.a: Something that counts the words in the sentence, any way Kiran liked.

qa.q: What was Kiran feeling while staring at the empty file?
qa.a: Kiran felt exposed and embarrassed after bragging, finding that sixty videos had not taught where to put "split" or "loop" 😰

qa.q: What would you change first in the way Kiran learns?
qa.a: Pause each video and write the same idea from scratch in a different form before moving on, so each lesson ends with Kiran's own code.

qa.q: How might Chetan bhaiya view the evening?
qa.a: He probably sees a keen learner who has been training the wrong muscle, and chooses to guide without laughing so Kiran keeps going.

grounding: Shows tutorial hopping failing: after many followed-along videos, a teen cannot write a small program in an empty file.
